newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean legislators pass divorce bill.
newsitem.headline: Chilean legislators pass divorce bill.

text.p: Chilean legislators early on Friday approved a bill that would open the way to legal divorce in their Roman Catholic country.
The bill, which is opposed by conservatives and the Roman Catholic church, was passed 53-40 in the Chamber of Deputies after two days of fiery debate.
"It's time to accept, with tolerance and respect, that some people's dogmas cannot be thrust upon the shoulders of others," legislator Ivan Moreira said.

The bill would lead to reform of Chile's 113-year-old civil code to make divorce legal. To become law, the bill must still pass the Senate, where rightists and military-appointed senators hold a majority and most are believed to oppose it.

Opponents of divorce also plan to challenge the law in the Constitutional Tribunal, a powerful judicial review body created by former military ruler Augusto Pinochet which can throw out proposals even before they become law.
A four-man majority of the seven-member tribunal was appointed by Pinochet before he left the presidency in 1990 and could rule the bill unconstitutional, legal experts say.

Divorce is illegal in only a handful of countries. It is a delicate issue in this country of conservative social mores, where abortion is a punishable offence and Hollywood films are regularly censored on cable television.
An appeals court this week banned the Martin Scorcese film "The Last Temptation of Christ" from being shown in Chile because it was deemed to run counter to religious values.
